structuredOutput.recommendation: Keep the Windows feature held. The HANDLE FileRenameInfo plan is the minimum correct operations set if RealBud fully bypasses Hermes atomic_replace/stage_write, recovers by digest and live identity rather than retrying ReplaceIfExists, and verifies the still-open source handle. RootDirectory plus source-HANDLE rename is documented and compatible with deny-delete sharing. WRITE_THROUGH plus FlushFileBuffers on that handle is the smallest documented NTFS metadata-flush request; MoveFileExW is not stronger; hardlinks are not worth extra states. Dual-rename CAS is not required for this cooperative-lock scope. Do not un-hold until process-kill tests exist. Power-loss durability remains unproved.

findings.issue: Hermes Windows persistence is incompatible with the hold: atomic_replace retries then _rewrite_in_place or _copy_fallback; fsync_directory is a no-op; stage_write can return an id after a failed persist. _write_file is that path.
findings.correction: Windows branch must persist already-rendered bytes only through CREATE_NEW plus source-HANDLE FileRenameInfo. Never call atomic_replace, _write_file, _rewrite_in_place, _copy_fallback, or stage_write. Signed intent exists only after readback of exact bytes/HMAC from the live object; failure returns no record and must not replace memory.

findings.issue: ReplaceIfExists=true plus crash/retry is the remaining correctness defect. Locks die with the process. A kill after a successful memory or receipt rename, or an ambiguous rename/flush, retried as replace, overwrites whatever now occupies the live name. Same for a second generated leaf after a successful no-clobber rename.
findings.correction: Recovery is reconcile, not replay. If live identity+digest matches after, write/keep final receipt only. If it still matches before and context matches, allow one replace. If the no-clobber leaf already matches this intent, that is success. Mismatch or unknown identity is conflict. Never blindly rename, never delete a recreated live name.

findings.issue: Design C understates post-rename sharing. The source handle keeps DELETE and GENERIC_WRITE (FlushFileBuffers requires GENERIC_WRITE). A second open is admitted only if its share mask allows every existing granted access, so FILE_SHARE_DELETE alone is insufficient; FILE_SHARE_WRITE is also required.
findings.correction: Prefer FileIdInfo plus HMAC on the still-live source handle and do not reopen. If a path open is used, request FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE|FILE_SHARE_DELETE and compare volume+file ID to the live source. Keep the source handle open until verification finishes.

findings.issue: ReplaceIfExists=true is not destination identity CAS (D1). An old target handle that denies DELETE blocks our replace (typically winerror 5). Sharing DELETE allows uncoordinated path substitution. Native .lock coordinates only participants on that lockfile identity (D11); msvcrt LK_LOCK is offset-based and retries up to 10s. Packet does not prove Windows O_NOFOLLOW/OPEN_REPARSE_POINT on the reused lock open.
findings.correction: Do not add claim-old-then-publish dual-rename for this scope; it creates a missing-target crash state the current recovery contract does not define. Document cooperative native writers, helper review lock, and private namespace. Dual-rename only if identity CAS against uncooperative same-SID writers becomes in-scope.

findings.issue: Parent pin and ACL claims are accurate only as stated in A/B, not as a child-namespace lock. Omitting FILE_SHARE_DELETE on directory handles pins those directory objects, not child names or FILE_DELETE_CHILD. PROTECTED_DACL blocks inheritance into the parent, not emission of its OI/CI ACEs. CreateFile on an existing name ignores the creation SD. NULL DACL grants everyone. Same-SID peers can still name children.
findings.correction: Treat parent pin as anti-directory-swap. Set a protected parent DACL with safe inheritable current-SID/SYSTEM/Administrators before CREATE_NEW; never NULL DACL. Verify every child by HANDLE (regular file, nlink=1, FileIdInfo, DACL) before private data. Reject unknown FS, remote/cloud/offline, and reparse ancestors.

findings.issue: winerror 5 is ambiguous: Hermes measured a held CPython target reader returns 5, and a real ACL denial is also 5. Classifying 5 as busy-only or ACL-only is wrong.
findings.correction: Bounded retry with fresh locks, FileIdInfo, type, nlink, and DACL checks. If still failing, preserve the signed journal and return busy/recovery-required. Do not native-fallback. Ambiguous rename/flush is resolved from signed disk state, not from the API return.

findings.issue: MoveFileExW and CreateHardLinkW look like durability or CAS shortcuts and are not. MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH’s explicit flush text is copy/delete; REPLACE_EXISTING is path-based; COPY_ALLOWED can copy and leave source. Hardlink then unlink can leave nlink=2, which current admission rejects.
findings.correction: Do not use MoveFileExW or CreateHardLinkW. Same-volume HANDLE FileRenameInfo only; generated FileName is a single leaf with no slash, colon, or ADS; SDK FILE_RENAME_INFO ABI, not the duplicated union in D1.

documentedLimits: D1: RootDirectory may resolve a relative FileName from a directory HANDLE; ReplaceIfExists=false fails if the target exists, true replaces it. No destination identity CAS. FileNameLength is UTF-16 bytes. Restrict to one leaf. Use SDK ABI.

D2: SetFileInformationByHandle operates on the opened source HANDLE. FileRenameInfo=3; FileDispositionInfo=4 needs DELETE. No cross-file transaction or durability is documented. Behavior varies by OS/filesystem.

D3: WRITE_THROUGH remarks say NTFS flushes metadata from the request, including rename; hardware write-through is not universal. Omitting FILE_SHARE_DELETE denies others’ DELETE/rename opens of that object. CREATE_NEW fails if the name exists. OPEN_REPARSE_POINT affects the final component only. Opening an existing file ignores the creation SD. BACKUP_SEMANTICS opens directories.
D4: FlushFileBuffers needs GENERIC_WRITE; volume flush needs admin. No POSIX directory-fsync equivalent.
D5: Metadata can remain cached without buffering; flush the file or use write-through. Power loss of cache is not process exit.
D6: MoveFileExW is path-based. WRITE_THROUGH wording does not establish HANDLE identity or cross-file journal order. Never COPY_ALLOWED.
D7: CreateHardLinkW is same-volume NTFS; links share the file SD. Interrupted hardlink+unlink can leave nlink=2.

D8/D9: HANDLE DACL set can propagate inheritable ACEs; existing explicit child ACEs need their own HANDLE check. PROTECTED_DACL blocks inbound inheritance only. NULL DACL is everyone. Sharing/MAXIMUM_ALLOWED can block propagation.
D10: Volume serial plus 128-bit file ID identifies two live handles. Persisted IDs are not proof after delete/reuse; keep the source handle live through verify.
D11: msvcrt LK_LOCK starts at the current offset, 1s retries, 10 attempts, and binds only the same lockfile identity.
Unproved: any Windows execution of this writer; hardware write-through; cross-file atomicity of intent then memory then receipt; directory-entry durability equal to POSIX fsync.
minimumWindowsTests: Process-kill after CREATE_NEW write+FlushFileBuffers and before rename: no live leaf, memory unchanged, no approval record.
Process-kill after no-clobber journal/proposal/claim rename and before readback: recovery accepts the existing leaf iff HMAC+FileIdInfo match this intent; must not mint a second leaf.
Process-kill after durable signed intent and before memory replace: memory digest still before; recovery may complete once or conflict; it must not replace unless before still matches.
Process-kill after memory ReplaceIfExists=true and before signed final receipt: if live digest is after, write receipt only; do not replace again.

Process-kill after final receipt and before pending claim/FileDispositionInfo: receipt remains; delete only the verified pending object via HANDLE rename-to-claim then disposition; a recreated live pending name is left in place.
Held target without FILE_SHARE_DELETE (CPython-style reader) on MEMORY.md: winerror 5, bounded retry, busy/recovery-required, bytes unchanged, no copy/truncate.

Our source handle denies FILE_SHARE_DELETE: foreign DELETE opens fail; our FileRenameInfo still succeeds; verify via live handle (and show that a verify-open without FILE_SHARE_WRITE fails while GENERIC_WRITE remains granted).
ReplaceIfExists=false when destination exists: fail closed. nlink≠1, reparse ancestor, non-NTFS/remote/cloud/offline: reject.
Instrumentation proof the Windows branch never calls os.replace, _rewrite_in_place, _copy_fallback, _write_file, or stage_write.
Do not treat power-pull as a release gate; WRITE_THROUGH+FlushFileBuffers is the requested NTFS flush, not a hardware or TxF guarantee.
